title: The broadcast guards refuse a wrong-chain payload, a codeless destination and denylisted calldata
notes: 0.32.0/0.33.0 broadcast guards. Every step is a guard REFUSAL, asserted through expectError — nothing here can reach a node. This is the only scenario that touches the SERVER's send path: `serverSign: true` makes the MCP sign as the keyring slot that owns the step's agent wallet (agent1 ← AGENT_PK_1) instead of the orchestrator signing a returned payload locally, which is the whole reason the 0.30–0.33 signer-side work has never been exercised by a swarm run. Step 4 is the important one: it routes the SAME denylisted bytes through dexe_proposal_create's `custom` branch, which copies caller-supplied action data verbatim and never touches PROPOSAL_BUILDERS — so it is the only step that reaches assertNoForbiddenCalldata INSIDE runBroadcastGuards, i.e. the copy that closed the 0.32.0 escape. Steps 1-3 hit dexe_tx_send, whose tool-local denylist pre-check fires before the shared guard. CAVEAT for step 4: proposal_create may emit approve/deposit legs before the create leg, and those would land (cents on 97) before the guard aborts the sequence — depend on S64 so the proposer already has deposited power and the create leg is the only payload. If DEXE_SIGNER_ALLOWLIST is set in the runner's env, B6 fires BEFORE B12 and these steps fail for the wrong reason; preflight prints which signer guards are armed.
